paragraphs.text: Our practice is dedicated to making sure that you receive the quality care you deserve. We focus on individualized, gentle, evidence-based orthodontic treatment for patients of all ages. We work as a team of doctors and specialists to design the right plan for each patient so you get excellent clinical results and leave every visit feeling cared for.
We strive to make every visit comfortable, efficient, and (yes) fun — creating an experience where patients feel welcomed and supported from first consult through final retention.

Kristen Alexander, DDS, MS provides comprehensive orthodontic care for children, teens, and adults. She combines evidence-based clinical techniques with a gentle chairside manner to create treatment plans tailored to each patient's needs and lifestyle.

image.alt: Dr. Kristen Alexander smiling in clinic

paragraphs.text: Dr. Alexander completed a Bachelor of Science in Microbiology/Immunology at the University of Rochester, earned her Doctorate of Dental Surgery with a minor in Pediatric Dentistry, magna cum laude, from SUNY at Buffalo School of Dental Medicine, and completed a Certificate of Proficiency in Orthodontics along with a Master of Science in Oral Biology at the University at Buffalo.

A Buffalo native, Dr. Alexander enjoys outdoor activities, travel, and cheering for the Sabres and Bills. She and her husband Joel are proud parents of two children. When she’s not in the office she likes to stay active and give back to the community.

Edwin L. Tyska, DDS has extensive experience in private practice and comprehensive orthodontic care. Dr. Tyska offers esthetic treatment options, surgical orthodontics, and dentofacial orthopedics, focusing on predictable, patient-centered results.

Dr. Tyska participates in continuing education to remain current on methods and materials and is a member of professional organizations including the Eighth District Orthodontic Academy, Northeastern Society of Orthodontists, American Association of Orthodontists, and the American Dental Association.

A resident of East Amherst, Dr. Tyska is active in the community as an assistant coach for the Lou Gehrig Lasers travel girls’ softball league. He enjoys golfing, traveling, and cheering on the Sabres. Dr. Tyska and his wife Courtney are parents to Landen and Aurora.

Get Started.title: What to expect at your first visit

paragraphs.text: At your complimentary orthodontic consultation you will meet our treatment coordinator for initial photos or scans, then meet with one of our doctors for a complete oral exam. The doctors consult together to design a customized treatment plan and then review that plan with you, including what’s involved, an estimated timeline, and recommended options.

Your visit typically begins with check-in and a review of your medical and dental history, followed by photos or digital scans and the doctor exam. We will discuss treatment choices, estimated timing, and financial options, and schedule next steps if you decide to move forward. Please bring completed patient forms when possible, your insurance card and photo ID, and any recent dental X-rays; if you do not have X-rays we will take the images needed.

image.alt: Orthodontic consultation in a bright office treatment room

paragraphs.text: We will review the cost of your individualized treatment and the payment plans available during your consultation. Our treatment coordinator will walk you through options so you can choose a plan that fits your budget.

Our practice accepts most major credit cards and most insurance plans, and our staff can assist with claims and paperwork. We also offer a secure online patient account for appointment reminders, payment history, and receipts. Ask about our complimentary consultation when you call or request an appointment online.

Please print and complete the appropriate health history form before your first appointment, or fill out your forms electronically using our secure online intake. Completing forms ahead of time helps us keep your visit efficient and focused on care.

paragraphs.text: Early treatment, often called Phase One, typically begins around age eight or nine and focuses on guiding jaw growth and making room for permanent teeth. Starting at the right time can simplify later care and reduce the need for more invasive treatment.
We commonly evaluate children by age seven to check growth patterns and bite development, then begin Phase One when intervention will best guide the jaws and emerging teeth.

image.alt: Young patient receiving early orthodontic intervention

paragraphs.text: Look for early or late loss of baby teeth, difficulty chewing, mouth breathing, persistent thumb-sucking, speech issues, protruding front teeth, or crowding by age seven or eight — any of these can indicate a need for evaluation.
Interceptive care can guide jaw growth, create space for permanent teeth, lower the risk of extractions, and sometimes eliminate or reduce the need for jaw surgery later in life.
It’s never too late to improve bite function and your smile. Adult treatment plans account for finished growth and often emphasize discreet, comfortable options that fit busy lives.

image.alt: Beautiful young Asian woman smiling and holding orthodontic retainer

paragraphs.text: Braces remain a reliable choice for many types of tooth movement. We offer both metal and ceramic options, and will recommend the system best suited to your goals and the clinical needs of your case.
Metal braces use brackets and archwires to apply precise, controlled forces. They are durable and effective for complex corrections, with periodic adjustments to guide movement.
Ceramic braces blend with tooth color for a less noticeable look. They work similarly to metal brackets but need careful hygiene and occasional precautions to avoid damage.

image.alt: Two stylish smiling teens taking selfie with braces

paragraphs.text: Invisalign<sup>®</sup> uses a series of custom clear aligners made from SmartTrack material and planned from precise 3D scans. Aligners are removable for eating and cleaning and are changed on a schedule to move teeth gradually.
The iTero scanner captures an accurate digital model so we can plan treatment precisely and show a virtual preview of expected results, helping you understand the proposed outcome before starting.

image.alt: Close-up of Invisalign aligners being placed on teeth

paragraphs.text: When skeletal jaw discrepancies cannot be corrected with braces or aligners alone, orthognathic surgery in coordination with orthodontic care can restore function and facial balance. We plan treatment in close collaboration with oral and maxillofacial surgeons for predictable outcomes.

image.alt: Orthodontic patient receiving orthognathic surgical consultation

paragraphs.text: Retainers keep teeth in their new positions after active treatment. We offer removable clear retainers, Hawley retainers, and bonded options and will recommend the right protocol to protect your results over time.

image.alt: Beautiful young Asian woman smiling and holding orthodontic retainer

paragraphs.text: We use modern digital tools to improve accuracy, comfort, and predictability. Digital scans, 3D treatment planning, and digital radiography help us design efficient, patient-friendly plans.
The iTero scanner captures fast, radiation-free 3D images for accurate records and precise aligner design without messy impressions.

image.alt: iTero digital scanner in use during orthodontic consultation

paragraphs.text: High-resolution digital radiography gives detailed imagery with lower exposure, supporting accurate diagnosis and treatment planning.

image.alt: Digital X-ray equipment showing detailed orthodontic imaging

paragraphs.text: Advanced software simulates each stage of tooth movement so you can preview likely results and we can map a precise, efficient path to your new smile.

paragraphs.text: Our greatest goal is to give you a healthy, straight, and beautiful smile. We understand that choosing to receive orthodontic care is a big decision, and this page answers common questions about treatment options, scheduling, insurance and payments, and home care so you can decide with confidence.

accordion.header: What treatment options do you offer?

paragraphs.text: We offer clear and metal braces for all ages, Invisalign<sup>®</sup> and Invisalign Teen® clear aligners, self‑ligating (Damon™) systems, removable appliances for minor tooth movement, surgical orthodontics and dentofacial orthopedics. Each treatment plan is customized to your needs, and the doctors consult together when designing your plan so you have experienced specialists collaborating on your care.

accordion.header: How long will treatment take and what affects treatment time?

paragraphs.text: Treatment time varies, often between one and three years, depending on age, the method selected, and the complexity of the case. Patient cooperation, such as wearing appliances, rubber bands, following retainer instructions, and maintaining good hygiene, has a major impact on treatment speed. Your doctor will discuss an estimated timeline when creating your customized plan.

accordion.header: What should I expect at the initial consultation and after?

paragraphs.text: The initial consultation includes a review of your dental and medical history, a complete oral exam, development of a customized treatment plan, and a discussion of financial and insurance options as well as payment plans. After the consultation we will schedule your first appointment; appliance placement appointments typically take about an hour.

image.alt: Orthodontic consultation in a bright office exam room

accordion.header: How do I schedule or change an appointment?

paragraphs.text: Contact the practice directly to schedule. Routine check visits during treatment are usually every four to eight weeks, and we will work with you to choose convenient days and times. If you need to reschedule or are running late, call the office and we will do our best to accommodate you. You can begin scheduling online at https://www.taortho.com/appointment-request.

accordion.header: What about insurance, payments, and financial questions?

paragraphs.text: Financial information, insurance options, and payment plans are reviewed during the initial consultation. The office will explain what your insurance covers and discuss available payment arrangements so you understand expected out-of-pocket costs.

accordion.header: What paperwork or forms do I need before my first visit?

paragraphs.text: Please complete patient information before your first appointment, either electronically or by printing and bringing the forms. Fill out forms electronically at https://patient.sesamecommunications.com/mandtortho/index.html. Downloadable intake PDFs are available: Child health history PDF at https://www.taortho.com/hub_sites/macdonald-andrew2/www/assets/uploads/files/health%20history(2).pdf and Adult health history PDF at https://www.taortho.com/hub_sites/macdonald-andrew2/www/assets/uploads/files/health%20history(3).pdf.

accordion.header: How should I care for my teeth and braces at home?

paragraphs.text: Brush and floss after every meal. Brush for two minutes with a soft-bristled or powered toothbrush at a 45 degree angle to the gum line, paying special attention around brackets and appliances. Use a floss threader or orthodontic floss, or ask about a water flosser, to clean between teeth and around wires. If soreness occurs after appliance placement, stick to a soft diet and rinse with warm salt water.

accordion.header: What should I do in an orthodontic emergency?

paragraphs.text: Many issues can be temporarily managed at home: use dental wax for poking wires, try to tuck a wire back into place with tweezers, and save a removable bracket in an envelope for your next visit. For severe pain or problems you can’t manage, call the office immediately so we can schedule an appointment to repair the appliance. Specific guidance for loose brackets, loose wires, poking wires, and general soreness is available in our emergency care instructions.
